candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: obtain specimens and monitor diagnostic/laboratory results, monitor clients receiving medications/treatments, and recognize potential complications related to therapy.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — therapeutic drug monitoring specimen timing
candidate.educational_objective: Collect an amikacin trough specimen immediately before the next scheduled dose so the result reflects the lowest serum concentration near the end of the dosing interval.

options.A: Immediately after the dose is administered.
options.C: Immediately before the next scheduled dose.
options.D: Only after amikacin therapy has been permanently discontinued.

candidate.rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories ordering guidance states that an amikacin trough specimen should be collected immediately before the next scheduled dose. A specimen collected soon after dosing represents a peak/post-dose context rather than a trough, and a midpoint specimen is not a trough. Therapeutic drug monitoring is performed during therapy, not only after permanent discontinuation. Therefore C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: An amikacin trough serum concentration should be collected immediately before the next scheduled dose.
candidate.source_document_title: Amikacin, Random, Serum (RAMIK) and Amikacin, Trough, Serum (TAMIK)
candidate.source_locator: RAMIK > Ordering Guidance: peak specimen 30-60 minutes after last dose; trough specimen immediately before next scheduled dose, order TAMIK. TAMIK > Useful For: monitoring adequate clearance near the end of a dosing cycle.
candidate.source_version_date: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories Test Catalog live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A provider orders an amikacin trough concentration. When should the serum specimen be collected?
